short: A British tailless delta-wing strategic bomber that formed the backbone of the United Kingdom's airborne nuclear deterrent.
full:
Introduced in 1956, the Avro Vulcan was one of Britain's three "V bombers" designed to carry nuclear weapons into the Soviet Union. Its striking, massive delta-wing design provided excellent high-altitude performance, high subsonic speed, and heavy payload capacity. As Soviet surface-to-air missile defenses improved in the 1960s, the Vulcan successfully adapted to a demanding low-level penetration role, replacing its free-fall nuclear bombs with the Blue Steel standoff missile.

The Vulcan's most famous operational deployment came near the end of its service life during the 1982 Falklands War. In the "Black Buck" raids, Vulcans flew immense 8,000-mile round trips from Ascension Island to bomb the airfield at Port Stanley, requiring extraordinarily complex aerial refueling operations. The aircraft was fully retired in 1984.
